title: Claude Fable 5.1 runs the forecast overnight
format_note: Narrative demo: a dashboard's overnight job is dramatised as abstract data animation, then the morning report and a chat follow-up. No speech, on-screen captions only.
one_thing: Claude does the night shift on 50,412 accounts and the human wakes to a report, asks one follow-up and clicks Mark as reviewed.

transcript.voice_style: No voice. Meaning is carried by serif title cards, mono captions and UI text.
transcript.script_shape: Setup (job scheduled), thesis card, what Claude reads and sorts overnight, forecast result, human follow-up in chat, sign-off tagline, product name, logo.

structure.frame0: Dark Goodcast Forecast dashboard on a slate-blue ground, a counter already rolling (48,37x) at 0 s; subject present, though text is small (f0001.jpg, strips/window-01-0s.jpg).
structure.first_3s: Account counter climbs to 50,412 by 0.29 s while KPIs fill in, then a push-in on the 'Claude · nightly forecast' pill: 'Scheduled 3:00 AM' (f0002.jpg, t=2s).

beats.what: Dashboard counter rolls to 50,412 with glow, KPIs and chart fade up.
Camera pushes to the Claude nightly-forecast pill; it turns orange and reads 'running nightly forecast', est 3h 10m.
Black card: 'Your team needs a forecast every morning. You trust Claude with the night shift.'
Circular lens over a collage of invoice, spreadsheet and contract; red marks overages. Caption: 'Overages four months running — and accelerating'.
Lens shrinks to an icon; grey and coloured circles with mono labels classify one account as LINEAR, ERRATIC, SEASONAL.
One orange stroke sweeps through hundreds of dots; a gate sorts them into five colour lanes: 'Sorting 50,412 accounts by consumption pattern'.
Lanes become five forecast curves with $ totals; 'Running 10,000 scenarios per cohort…' then weighting by revenue share.
Orange line wipes the ground from black to cream and becomes the dashed P50 forecast with P10/P90 band.
Light dashboard resolves: 50,412 accounts, Q3 P50 $64,232,806, spread 8.8%, locked in $35.3M.
Report 'Q3: how much is locked in vs modeled?', Claude Fable 5.1 chat answers a CFO backtest request, chart added, cursor clicks Mark as reviewed.
Cream card: 'Run by Claude.' then 'Led by you.'
Cream card with the product name 'Fable 5.1', which drifts up slightly.
Claude starburst and wordmark on cream; audio silent from 72.5 s.

hero_moment.what: Lens fully open on the document collage with red overage circle and '105,838.42' (f0006.jpg); final cut of the film's only burst.

ending.cta_text: Run by Claude. Led by you.
ending.what: Tagline, product name and logo on separate cream cards, each in the same centred serif, no URL or button.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: One burst of five cuts in 3.7 s at 8.4-12.1 s, then a single 49.7 s shot (66.8% of runtime, 16.12-65.83 s) in which dots, curves, ground colour and UI morph into each other without cuts.

look.ground: Black or near-black for the first 41 s, then warm cream (#faf8f3 area) with a teal-to-peach gradient behind the light UI; end cards cream.
look.accent_use: Terracotta orange is the single actor: the stroke, gate, forecast line and highlighted words; five muted category colours appear only as data.
look.type: Warm serif for titles and end cards; grotesk sans for UI and captions; small italic sans caption with starburst; monospace for data captions with one orange word.

look.depth: Flat graphic layers plus soft drop shadow on the app window; one lens mask; background circles at differing opacity give mild parallax in the 12-16 s section.

product_ui.camera_on_ui: Push-in on the status pill (1-5 s), then a slow drift and zoom through the report and chat panel (46-66 s); window crops off-screen while the camera follows the action.
product_ui.notes: Invented Goodcast app, not Claude's product. Body text in the report is about 15 px of 720 (2.1%) and chat text about 14 px; the drift keeps the active region large. Mono captions measure 17 px (2.4%), below the 2.6% rule.

motion.text_entry: Counter digits roll with glow at 0 s; serif card appears whole, exits by a horizontal stretch at 8.42 s (strips/window-05-8.417s.jpg); end card words fade and the tagline narrows to 'Led by you.' then letters of 'Fable' type on (strips/window-36-68.167s.jpg).
motion.ui_motion: Chat reply types out ('Anything' at t=56 becomes the full question with three chips at t=60); stroke-drawn cursor moves along the chart and presses the button; KPI numbers count up.
motion.camera: Constant slow pushes and drifts on the UI; the abstract middle uses lateral travel with the dot field. Camera never stops except on cards.
motion.eases: Not measured from curves; strips show smooth deceleration on push-ins and an abrupt hard stretch on the title exit.

good.observation: A single orange stroke is the continuous actor from 16 s to 46 s, turning into each metaphor in turn and linking black abstraction to the cream UI.
The abstract section proves the one capability: 50,412 dots sorted into five behaviours that become five forecast curves, with the numbers on screen.
A restrained sentence structure ends the film: three centred serif cards (tagline, product, logo) each take its own beat on one cream ground.
The follow-up exchange is concrete: a CFO request, a numeric answer (6.6%, 8.9% to 5.4%) and the chart added under the forecast, finishing on a click.
The first frame already shows the product subject with a counter in motion, and 0.3 s later reads 50,412.

rule_candidates.rule: Carry one accent-coloured object from scene to scene (stroke becomes gate, then forecast line) so a 30 s abstract section reads as one gesture without cuts.
rule_candidates.evidence: orange stroke at f0011-f0023; longest shot 49.7 s, 66.8% of runtime

rule_candidates.rule: A film can run without cuts for two thirds of its runtime if something on screen morphs every 2-4 s; cuts-per-minute is then 5.7, not 17-33.
When the product is shown, change the ground from dark to light at the moment the result arrives (black to cream at 41-46 s).
Put the burst of cuts early (8.4-12.1 s, 11-16% of length) when the film spends its second half on one long shot; the hero sits at its end.
End on three separate centred serif cards (tagline 2.7 s, product 2.9 s, logo about 2.8 s) rather than one stacked lockup; logo hold at least 2.8 s.
A mono caption that explains a data animation stays at 2.6% of height or more; at 2.4% the captions in this film are the weakest legible element.
Put one concrete user request and a numeric answer inside the UI chat (CFO asks for a backtest; answer 6.6%) so the product proves itself in one exchange.
Open on a product screen with a rolling counter so frame 0 holds the subject and the key number lands by 0.3 s.
